messages.content: What is the dominant genetic trait of a Lion?

message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult males. The gene responsible for mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion—if a male lion inherits at least one copy of the allele that promotes mane growth, he will develop a mane (though its size and density can vary). This dominant trait is what distinguishes male lions from females, who typically lack a mane.
